To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
web research is a valid method for conducting psychological studies, but the adoption of web-based research in the curriculum has been slow and inconsistent.

the web has become the primary means for conducting psychological research, that there is a lack of awareness of the issues that are unique to web research, that this lack of awareness is reflected in the design and conduct (and reporting) of web-based studies, and that the lack of education about web-based research in psychology curricula is a contributing factor to these problems.

web-based research is a viable method of psychological research, that it is not well understood by students or researchers, that it is often conducted with a laxness that may be problematic, and that there is no clear way to educate students and researchers about the nature of research on the Web.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two issues.
the state of research on the internet. We have found that there is a large amount of research conducted online, and it is increasing rapidly.
how researchers are currently using the web for research, and what can be done to improve their understanding of the unique challenges of web-based research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the web can support valid psychological research, but that there is a need to develop a coherent and comprehensive approach to teaching web research methods. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2016 APA, all rights reserved)
there are a number of issues that need to be resolved before web research is a mature and robust method for conducting psychological research.
there is a need for more education of researchers in the unique features of conducting research online.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the web is an excellent method for conducting research, but that there is a need for education in the unique features of research on the internet.
the field of web-based research has come a long way in the last 20 years, but there is still a long way to go.

there is a lack of awareness of the unique aspects of web-based research, a lack of training for researchers in the conduct of web-based research and a lack of awareness that the web is a valid method for conducting psychological research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to develop a set of guidelines for the conduct of web-based research, and to include these guidelines in psychology curricula.
there is a need for more education about conducting research online and that the web can and should be used as a method for teaching research methods.
web research is not a panacea for the conduct of research, nor is it a replacement for other forms of data collection.
